title: Make the session sweeper safe to run beside live requests

blocks.text: The login service keeps the time each session was last seen in a `Collections.synchronizedMap`. Every request calls `touch`, so the map changes many times a second. Once a minute a sweeper removes the sessions that have expired, and on busy days it dies with `ConcurrentModificationException`, leaving stale sessions behind. The debug endpoint that dumps the sessions has a problem of its own: the dump it is writing out changes while it writes.

items: `sweep(policy)`: remove every session the policy says has expired, and return their ids;
`snapshot()`: the sessions as they are now, in a map that later requests don't change.

blocks.text: When you're done, a sweep finishes however many requests arrive while it runs, a request that arrives during a sweep is kept, and a dump doesn't change once it is taken. About ten lines in total.
The tests send a request into the middle of a sweep, through the expiry policy, and check from the JVM's thread data whether the request had to wait for the sweep.

cases.says: a sweep removes and returns the sessions the policy calls expired, keeps the others, and a snapshot shows what is left
a request that touches a session while the sweep walks the map waits until the walk is over
touches made after a snapshot was taken don't show in it

origin.section: Walking a Wrapper Is Many Calls: Hold the Wrapper's Lock for the Whole Walk

concepts: Walking a synchronized wrapper is many calls; the walk holds the wrapper's own lock throughout, and every writer waits for it.
